_how_to_use: 406 JPEGs carved from a 119-page PDF of GCR trade reviews.
The PDF has almost no text layer (137 chars), so the content IS the images.
Tweet screenshots here are NOT all present in gcr_archive.txt - spot-checked
'fade listing pumps' (IOTX/TRU/CLV/MNGO/AXS) appears only in the images.
Review is incremental: set reviewed=true and fill notes as images are read.
'kind' is aspect-ratio guesswork; 'content' on a reviewed image is the truth (img001 is a header painting the ratio called a tweet).

Blotters are the highest-value images and CANNOT be found by pixel heuristics: they run 1 row to 9, light (Binance) and dark (FTX). A filter tuned on three light blotters missed img335 entirely. Use scripts/contact_sheets.py and look.

images.notes: NOT a tweet — a Twitter header painting (1500x500 is the 3:1 header ratio). No trading content. Shows the aspect-ratio classifier cannot separate headers from tweet screenshots; treat 'tweet_screenshot' as a hint, not a fact.

THE SOURCE of the discarded hedged_book check, found. May 13: 'If you're longing specific alts right now [whether due: asymmetric information edge, strong intuition, catalysts, or even technical analysis], you would be wise to find hedges to mitigate your broader market risk. Consider shorting weaker alts against your favorite plays.' It is ADVICE TO OTHERS about a specific situation — longing alts — not a description of his own standing book. Reading it as the latter is what produced the false CONTRADICTS.
